# remote_file_tool

> Read, write, patch, or delete files on a remote code workspace via SSH.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | `developer` |
| Callable | MCP clients; in-app @ai conversations; grantable to agents |
| Filter | `https://www.dsiloed.com/api/v1/mcp?tools=remote_file_tool` |

## Description

This is the description the server sends to the model, verbatim.

Read, write, patch, or delete files on a remote code workspace via SSH.

IMPORTANT: Always use this tool for file modifications — do NOT use remote_shell_tool
with sed, awk, ruby -e, or similar commands to edit files. This tool handles all file
operations reliably.

Operations:
- read: Read a file's contents
- write: Write content to a file (creates parent directories). For edits, read the
  file first, modify the content, then write the full file back.
- patch: Insert text after a matching line (useful for adding routes, config entries, etc.)
- delete: Delete a file

All paths are relative to the workspace's working directory.

EXAMPLES:

Read a file:
{workspace_slug: "my-project", operation: "read", file_path: "app/models/user.rb"}

Write a file:
{workspace_slug: "my-project", operation: "write", file_path: "app/models/widget.rb",
 content: "class Widget < ApplicationRecord\nend\n"}

Insert a line after a match (patch):
{workspace_slug: "my-project", operation: "patch", file_path: "config/routes.rb",
 match: "get 'healthy', to: 'health_check#healthy'",
 content: "      get 'dev_team_test', to: 'dev_team_test#show'"}

Delete a file:
{workspace_slug: "my-project", operation: "delete", file_path: "tmp/debug.log"}

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_slug` | string | yes | Workspace slug identifying which remote server to connect to. |
| `operation` | string | yes | File operation to perform. One of: `read`, `write`, `patch`, `delete`. |
| `file_path` | string | yes | Relative path to the file within the workspace working directory. |
| `content` | string | no | File content (required for write/patch). For patch, this is the text to insert after the match. |
| `match` | string | no | For patch operation: the line to match (inserts content after this line). Must match exactly. |
